utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the Case Number IT-98-29-A, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Could I please have the appearances of the parties. The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Helen Brady appearing for the Prosecution, together with Michelle Jarvis and our case manager, Kim Fischer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brady. Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of the Defence -- good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Defence of General Stanislav Galic, Mara Pilipovic, attorney-at-law, and my colleague, Mr. Stephane Piletta-Zanin. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Galic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Thank you, I am following the proceedings in a language I understand and I am doing it quite well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I am glad to hear that. You may be seated. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on 2 March 2006. Mr. Galic, again, could you please rise? I would like to ask you whether you have any issues that you would like to raise at this time, and in particular regarding your mental or physical well being.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to say a few words, by your leave. First of all, I would like to thank you -- I would like to thank you personally, since you have been in charge of the proceedings at this stage, that you have been inquiring of my health. On the 2nd of March we had our last Status Conference, and I saw then that already by the 6th of March I was supposed to sign a document for handing over my medical documentation here to the Tribunal. I indeed signed it. So by your leave I'm talking about what happened in between since the last Status Conference. On the 9th of March, I immediately underwent some treatment -- actually, a punction at a special hospital. This is a physiotherapy that is going on and this is the fourth time I have undergone this therapy. Last time it was so painful that I really would not want to have it repeated again, but I'm told that it won't be that painful any longer because this -- or rather, the pain is caused by touching the spinal nerve. So you will appreciate how painful that is. Since then I have been a bit better, so I guess that the treatment has a certain favourable effect. I don't know what you've been told about the condition of my health, but once again I would like to underline that during my arrest I was terrorised in an awful way. I hope that my lawyers will manage to get some documents about that and that they will present them, namely that the persons who committed this terror actually admit to it. For six months I couldn't walk; as you know, I had to use crutches. And my teeth were punched out. I had an operation of my left arm and my left shoulder has been hurt and you can still see it. For seven years now I've been undergoing therapy for my spine. And, believe me, all of that is not easy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I do hope that you will get better and you will not have to have those painful treatments again. Does the Prosecutor have any comments on what Mr. Galic said?

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. The parties' submissions on the respective appeal of the trial judgement are now complete. As the parties are aware oral argument on the appeals will be held on Tuesday, 29 August 2006 in Courtroom I. The Appeals Chamber plans later this summer to file an order letting the parties know the timetable for this hearing. This morning the Prosecution filed a status report concerning the archive of military documents recently compiled by the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the Prosecution's status report, it stated that the parties may be able to advise the Chamber today of their respective positions in relation to this archive. So I want to ask the parties whether they anticipate filing any motions as a result of the fact that materials in this archive are available. Obviously, if a party would want to introduce material from this archive, it would need to file a Rule 115 motion. Ms. Brady, do you think that the Prosecution will be filing any motions as a result of the fact that materials in this archive are available?

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I can say that we don't anticipate making any filings, but as I indicated in the status report, this information has only recently come to our attention. We've made efforts to firstly inform the Defence of the material and its accessibility to the Defence. We've also made some preliminary steps in ascertaining the parameters of the material and what's in the collection. At this stage I can anticipate that we will not, but there is a caveat on it in terms of not having properly researched the material. I also, Your Honour, would bear in mind that our position also is affected by what -- Mr. Galic, what his Defence team does, if anything, with the material because in terms of 115 we would have to consider our position in terms of rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Brady. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Allow me to answer instead of Madam Pilipovic. Indeed we had talks with the opposite party and we were able to speak with General Galic about this new situation, new to him. At this stage of the proceedings, I believe it is better and proper to do the following as early as next week, Tuesday and Wednesday, provided everything is put in one single place. It could be Banja Luka. Mara Pilipovic is planning to go to Banja Luka to get in touch with the appropriate people, will endeavour to look at all the documents in as far as it is possible to see; once that is done, it can be done in terms of proceedings. At this stage we still do not know whether we are going to have production of new evidence under Rule 115, but we're going to rush to Banja Luka in order to speed up the proceedings as much as we can, and I think that by two weeks -- yes, is that right? What do you think? Yes, within two or three weeks we should be able to give you an idea to the Prosecution, to you, and to your Appeals Chamber, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just emphasise that if either party would want to move any motions, I would certainly encourage that party to avoid any delays, any unwarranted delays about our scheduling of the hearing, and I am quite sure that Mr. Galic is quite anxious to have his case tried. Before concluding the Status Conference, I want to ask counsel for the Prosecution and Defence whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Ms. Brady.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Your Honour, you mentioned that shortly Your Honour would issue a further scheduling order in relation to the hearing. On the last occasion Your Honour mentioned the list of issues or questions that the Appeals Chamber may be particularly interested in, and I would like to ask Your Honour if in that further scheduling order such a list of issues will be contained; and if it is, then of course both parties would very much appreciate having it as soon as we could in order to facilitate our preparations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Of course this will be for the entire Bench to decide. I appreciate your interest in having such a list of issues as soon as possible, and my own assumption is that we will have that in the scheduling order. Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. To echo what the Prosecution just said, and sometimes we are able to agree with the Prosecution, then -- I'm not sure -- this -- remembering now that we were talking about a deadline of six weeks ante deum in order to get ready. I'm not speaking on my own behalf, but some may plan holidays with their families and it would be useful -- I can see the Prosecution nodding. It would be easier for everybody to organise themselves and their work on either side of the well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, I appreciate your comments. If there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance and call these proceedings to a halt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.45 p.m.
